env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

[!exec:patch] skip 'patch unavailable'

cd m
go run .
cp stdout $WORK/go-output
cp main.go $WORK/main.orig

# --fix emits the patch alone on stdout and leaves the tree untouched.
logos next --fix
cp stdout $WORK/fix.patch
! grep '^logos next' $WORK/fix.patch
grep '^\+\+\+ .*main\.lgo' $WORK/fix.patch
! exists main.lgo
! exists next_tasks.json
cmp main.go $WORK/main.orig

# Each call is convertible on its own, and together they are the file's
# only fmt uses, so the fixer must not produce a patch that orphans the
# fmt import. Whatever safe mix it chooses (rewrite some and keep a use,
# or keep every call and report it), the applied result must build and
# behave exactly like the original program.
exec patch --batch --fuzz=0 -p1 -i $WORK/fix.patch
! exists main.go
exists main.lgo
logos build ./...
logos run .
cmp stdout $WORK/go-output

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/nextmultifmt

go 1.27
-- m/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

func status(ok bool) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("ready=%t", ok)
}

func summary(n int, name string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("count=%d item=%s", n, name)
}

func main() {
	if _, err := os.Stdout.WriteString(status(true) + "\n" + summary(3, "bolt") + "\n"); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
